title: VLUN: a provenance-preserving smart-contract security reasoning dataset
description: A provenance-preserving corpus of smart-contract security findings across Solidity, Rust, Move, Cairo, Circom, Noir, Leo, TypeScript, Go, Vyper and Clarity. Every record traces to a public artefact and every claim carries its evidence type. Governing rule: truth over scale; unknown is a counted outcome. The licence is scoped, not blanket: this project grants MIT over its own code and CC BY 4.0 over its own documents and data, and only for the paths RELEASE_MANIFEST.json lists with a released rights status. The evidence corpus and every piece of third-party material are not licensed here at all, and attribution is not a redistribution right (see LICENSE and NOTICE.md).

rights.released_set_rule: a tracked path that is not listed in RELEASE_MANIFEST.json with a released rights status is not licensed here, and this project grants no redistribution right over it

licences_of_released_paths.note: these are the licences of the released paths only. The per-path statement is RELEASE_MANIFEST.json's `path_licences`; no third-party material is licensed here, wherever it occurs.

notes: There is no single repository-wide licence: the licence is per path, and RELEASE_MANIFEST.json is the authoritative statement of what may be redistributed. Fill the deposition's licence field from that manifest's `path_licences` for the released paths, and do not claim a licence over the evidence corpus. DOI is minted by Zenodo on first publish (see docs/ARCHIVAL.md). After publishing, copy the DOI back into CITATION.cff (doi: + preferred-citation.doi) and regenerate the README so the citable artifact is pinned in-repo.
